title: Hifiman Ananda Headphones US$160.99 (~A$231) Delivered @ Hifiman Local Store via AliExpress
body:
Deal: Hifiman Ananda Headphones US$160.99 (~A$231) Delivered @ Hifiman Local Store via AliExpress

[dottjt] Just my thoughts on getting the Edition XS recently but… I didn't love it. I think these Hifiman headphones are very overhyped, especially if you're used to something like the HD 600. The Hifiman just sounds muddled.
It could also be that I recently got a proper L/R speaker setup with a quality sub and now headphones just sound pitiful in comparison.
[Lps] Mate, you got a dud XS - return them for replacement. I have access to the best studio speakers out there and am yet to find a set that sound as good as my Hifiman XS.
[maverickjohn] With a good dac/amp they are quite awesome. Did you buy from genuine hifiman store?
Headphones are very much personal preference but still seems like an unfortunate outcome for you
[dottjt] I bought them from this very aliexpress store.
I think starting with the HD 600, the one thing I really didn't like about the Edition XS was the lack of vocal clarity. It did everything else great, but without that clarity it just felt… hollow. Reading about it online, basically at this price point it's a compromise. LIke you're going to get one or the other, unless you go a few tiers up.
[maverickjohn] Fair enough. I found it very much depended on the song.
When I listen to Whitney on the edition xs the vocal clarity is very pronounced. But if I listen to a instrument heavy song, the vocals are not as clear.
As the bass does dampen the vocals a little. I found them generally favourable for my style of music and also really good for ps5 gaming.
[Brotality] I was curious about Planars and I very recently got a Fiio FT1 Pro next to my HD6XX.
My experience is very similar to yours, even tho the FT1 Pro is most commonly reviewed as the Planars closest sounding to the HD6XX.
The dip in the mids and the higher bass, drown the vocals substantially. Especially in songs that have electric guitars.
I have grown to appreciate the different sound signature, but I would pick the HD6XX over the planars any day of the week.
[itchy scratchy] @Brotality: I did the exact same thing, grabbed a pair of FT1 Pro to have something different to my 6XX.
It's so close to sounding good I needed to EQ back the 1.6K dip and calm some peaks in 3/5K before I was happy.
Without doing that, I just can't get used to how some instruments sound. Almost like hollow/metallic.
I can definitely see their place, though. Especially since planars are getting much cheaper compared to a couple of years ago, and they offer a lot.
I've owned the Edition XS and Ananda Nano before, and while pretty great, there was always something about them that kept me from using them as much as I wanted (mainly the size lol).
These days I hardly use headphones (if I do, I still reach for 6XX) and daily my IEMs instead.
[congo] I ordered the Hifiman HE400se from this store:
https://www.aliexpress.com/store/912342929
I think it was a dud.
[ReaperX22] I've had the Edition XS for almost 3 years and they're amazing. Running off an ifi zen dac, with xbass enabled which, imo, helps it a lot for me but I enjoy bass, despite it being already slightly v shaped.
That said, Hd600 being quite neutral you'd probably just find the planar to be overwhelming as well as 'muddled' because you're expecting that more flat curve. You're probably comparing and missing the mids. I went from shure srh1840 to these and these are way fuller but the 1840s are clearer (albeit, imo, a little boring sometimes)
What speakers/sub did you you get out of curiosity?
[dottjt] It's just missing that vocal clarity from the HD 600 that I love, and it's hard to go without it now.
I got the Elac Debut 3.0 B6.3 + RSL 10E. Absolutely heavenly. Just an absurd amount of detail and the sub ties it all perfectly. You just don't get that level detail from headphones, especially with the sub.

[rzy6cn] HIFIMAN is a terrible company when it comes to pricing. They seem to have no control over the resale value of their products, so if you decide to sell the headphones later, you may find they are worth almost nothing.
For example, when the HE-R10D launched in 2021, it sold for around USD 1,300/AUD 1,800. By 2025, the price had dropped to about USD 150 / AUD 220. In comparison, a Sennheiser headphone may lose only 20–30% of its value even over many years.
HIFIMAN can offer such extreme discounts because the manufacturing cost is probably only a small fraction of the original retail price. So I would never buy from them unless I was prepared to treat the headphones as a disposable, one-time purchase with little or no resale value.
[heef] Since when did anyone expect a pair of Chi-Fi cans to hold their value like a Toyota?
Just delay your upgrade cycle so that you are getting a good deal every time. That's the OzBargain way.
[rzy6cn] This has nothing to do with where the company is based. Any manufacturer selling premium-priced hi-fi products should understand the importance of channel management and price control. If the same product can be purchased through different channels at 2,000 AUD and 1,000 AUD at the same time (and probably 300 AUD after 2 years), that's a clear failure of pricing strategy. It severely damages consumer confidence and unfairly penalizes customers who paid full price. A company that cannot maintain reasonable pricing discipline inevitably destroys the resale value of its own products, and ultimately hurts the very customers who supported the brand.
[heef] You may see it as a 'failure of pricing strategy'.
I see it as the natural rate of technology becoming more affordable and available to the masses. This is a win for 99% of people.
It most certainly is to do with where the company is based. Look at EVs. It is their strategy. Do things cheaper, and inevitably do things better (I don't own one, just an observation e.g. battery tech).
